page.layout: Two round coin medallions with legends across the top, side by side (left: Scribonia, right: Livia Drusilla), both illustrations. Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs. Below the text, the gathering signature. At the foot of the page, a decorative woodcut ornament (no text).

main_text.p: SCRIBONIA Imperatoris Augusti vxor fuit, postquàm ille dimisisset supradictâ Claudiam, quæ illi in matrimonium pacta fuerat, sicuti diximus. Porrò Scribonia hæc nupserat ante duobus Consularibus, & ex altero quoque mater fuerat: cum hac etiâ diuortium fecit Augustus, pertæsus (vt scripsit) morum eius peruersitatem: ex hac filiam Iuliam suscepit. Vide C. Suetonium Tranquillum in vita Octauij Augusti, Romanorum imperatoris secundi.

LIVIA Drusilla vxor quoque fuit Augusti, quam matrimonio Tiberij Neronis, Imperatoris Tiberij patris, & quidem prægnantem abduxit, dilexitque ac probauit vnice ac perseueranter. Ex hac nullos suscepit liberos, cùm maximè cuperet: infans (is est Drusus Tiberij Imperatoris frater, ac Claudij Cæsaris, qui Tiberio successit, pater) qui conceptus erat, immaturus est editus. in oculis Liuiæ, & in hac voce defecit Augustus: Liuia, nostri coniugij memor viue, ac vale: fortitus exitum facilem, & qualem semper optauerat. Vide Suetonium Tranquillum in Octauio Augusto, & secudi libri huius operis paginâ quintam.

page.notes: The two coin medallions are illustrations (portrait profiles of Scribonia and Livia Drusilla); their circular legends are transcribed above as lines. The woodcut ornament at the foot of the page is an illustration with no text. "Mm 4" is the gathering signature. "secudi" is printed that way. The italic sentence "Liuia, nostri coniugij memor viue, ac vale:" is set in italic in the original.
